notes: Same Source-engine (srcds) binaries and therefore the same stock admin set as every other Source 2013 multiplayer game; the game/mod directory is hl1mp (srcds_run -game hl1mp). RCON is TCP on the game port (default 27015, set with -port) and is enabled by setting rcon_password in hl1mp/cfg/server.cfg. status is both info and roster, printing header lines then one '# userid [slot] "name" STEAM_x:y:z ...' line per player, so playerParse is regex. kickid accepts a userid or a Steam ID plus a message; the engine usage string for bans is 'banid < minutes > < userid | uniqueid > { kick }', where {duration} is MINUTES, 0 means permanent, and the trailing literal kick ejects a connected player. banid takes no reason argument. Bans live in memory until writeid rewrites hl1mp/cfg/banned_user.cfg (lines of the form 'banid 0 STEAM_0:1:123456'; older engines write a float duration), and server.cfg conventionally carries 'exec banned_user.cfg' and 'writeid'. removeid unbans live, again needing writeid to persist. No motd command exists - the MOTD is the file named by the motdfile cvar (hl1mp/motd.txt) - so motd is omitted. CONFIDENCE IS LOW DELIBERATELY: the server's identity (app id 255470, -game hl1mp) is confirmed by three independent sources, but no Half-Life Deathmatch: Source specific console/cvar listing could be found. Every command here is taken from engine-level Source documentation and from the HL2DM cvar dump for the sibling game on the same engine branch, not from a source about this game. No source contradicts it, but nothing game-specific confirms it either; one run against a live hl1mp server would move this to high.
